item.title: Product-stabilized filamentation by human glutamine synthetase allosterically tunes metabolic activity
item.description: To maintain metabolic homeostasis, enzymes must adapt to fluctuating nutrient levels through mechanisms beyond gene expression. Here, we demonstrate that human glutamine synthetase (GS) can reversibly polymerize into filaments aided by a composite binding site formed at the filament interface by the product, glutamine. Time-resolved cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) confirms that glutamine binding stabilizes these filaments, which in turn exhibit reduced catalytic specificity for ammonia at...

item.title: Salivary Cutaneous Fistula Caused by Submandibular Sialolithiasis in an Adolescent
item.description: Pediatric submandibular sialolithiasis with a salivary cutaneous fistula is exceptionally rare. A 15-year-old boy presented with a 4-month history of a persistent right submandibular inflammatory lesion with a central opening and hypergranulation despite previous incision and drainage. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated a 10.8 mm distal Wharton duct stone, a 34 mm inflammatory lesion extending toward the skin, and marked atrophy of the right submandibular gland. Because of...

item.title: Renal stress-associated extracellular vesicle signaling linked to lysosomal cathepsin D and NEK7-NLRP3 neuroinflammation
item.description: Systemic exposure to neurotoxins such as 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) affects both the central nervous system (CNS) and peripheral organs; however, the contribution of peripheral organ stress to neuroinflammation remains incompletely understood. Here, we propose a peripheral-to-central signaling mechanism in which renal stress-associated extracellular vesicles (EVs) are linked to microglial inflammasome activation. Using computational and biochemical approaches, cathepsin...

item.title: Comparative Diagnostic Performance of Three Commercial Real-Time PCR Assays for the Detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Complex in Bronchial Washing Specimens: A Large Retrospective Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort with a high proportion of smear-negative cases, the Cobas and Xpert assays exhibited significantly higher sensitivity for MTBC detection than the AdvanSure assay. These findings highlight the importance of highly sensitive molecular assays for the early diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis, particularly in patients with low bacillary burden.

item.title: Secondary Metabolites from the Marine-Derived Fungus Aspergillus udagawae SFC20170619-M03 Exhibiting Disease Control Activity
item.description: In our screening program for novel biocontrol agents, we found that the culture filtrate of the marine-derived fungus Aspergillus udagawae SFC20170619-M03 exhibited disease control activity against several fungal plant diseases, including tomato gray mold, tomato late blight, and pepper anthracnose. Bioassay-guided fractionation of the active extracts led to the isolation of sixteen secondary metabolites, comprising nine xanthones (1-9), three benzoquinones (10-12), three spirocyclic furanone...

item.title: Vagal sensing of altered gut microbiota links to externalizing behaviors
item.description: Interoceptive brain responses triggered by intestinal microbiota influence mood-related behaviors such as anxiety and depression. Although genetic mutations can alter the gut microbiome, how alterations in the gut microbiome associated with host genetic variations relate to behavioral outcomes is not fully understood. We investigated how Sirtuin 3 (Sirt3) deficiency is linked to altered gut-brain interactions and mood-related behaviors. Gut microbiota composition and behavior were compared...

item.title: Interfacial microenvironments enable abiotic ribonucleoside formation in micro- and nanoscale compartments
item.description: The abiotic emergence of ribonucleosides remains a central challenge in origin-of-life research because ribonucleosides form inefficiently and are often unstable under prebiotically plausible conditions. Here we show that interfacial microenvironments within aqueous micro- and nanoscale compartments containing D-ribose, phosphoric acid, and nucleobases promote ribonucleoside formation by creating reaction-permissive physicochemical conditions independent of the specific compartment type. Across...

item.title: Prolonged Donor Warm Ischemia in Pure Laparoscopic Donor Right Hepatectomy Is Associated With Increased Recipient Biliary Stricture Risk: A Retrospective Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged DWIT appears to increase the risk of recipient biliary strictures, suggesting that minimizing DWIT in laparoscopic donor hepatectomy could help optimize outcomes.

item.title: Global Incidence of All-Cause Dementia: A Meta-Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The harmonized estimates presented in this study provide a comparable benchmark for global dementia incidence and inform planning for prevention, diagnosis, and memory-care services, particularly in underrepresented low- and middle-income country settings.

item.title: Depression and Anxiety Risk in Children With Intellectual Developmental Disorder
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This nationwide cohort study of more than 236 000 children and adolescents found that individuals with IDD, particularly males, younger children, and those with mild comorbidity burden, had increased depression and anxiety risks compared with individuals without developmental disorders. These findings underscore the need for targeted screening and interventions tailored to sociodemographic and comorbidity profiles.

item.title: Understanding and clinical approach to early T-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia
item.description: Early T-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ETP-ALL) is a distinct biological subtype of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) that was first described in 2009 based on a gene expression profile resembling that of early T-cell precursors in the thymus. ETP-ALL is characterized by an immature immunophenotype featuring positivity for CD7 and cytoplasmic CD3, with co-expression of myeloid/stem cell markers, and absence of CD1a, CD8, with weak or absent CD5 expression. ETP-ALL...

item.title: Predictive value of left ventricular <sup>18</sup>F-FDG PET/CT derived parameters and uptake patterns for chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity in patients with lymphoma
item.description: CONCLUSION: Routine post-treatment oncologic FDG PET/CT may provide exploratory information on myocardial metabolic changes associated with CTRCD in lymphoma patients receiving anthracycline-based chemotherapy. Although quantitative PET parameters differed between patients with and without CTRCD, the focal/diffuse myocardial uptake pattern was the only imaging variable that remained independently associated with CTRCD after multivariable adjustment. These findings should be considered...

item.title: Regulating the packing of π-conjugated ligands toward exceptional birefringence in magnesium phosphite hybrids
item.description: Developing phosphite-based birefringent materials with simultaneously large birefringence and wide optical transparency remains a significant challenge. Inspired by the large intrinsic polarizability anisotropy of planar π-conjugated ligands, we introduced 1,10-phenanthroline (phen) into the magnesium phosphite system to explore the influence of ligand packing on birefringence. Colorless crystals of Mg(phen)(HPO(3)) (1) and Mg(phen)(H(2)PO(3))(2)·H(2)O (2) were successfully obtained under...

item.title: Competency Scale for Developmentally Supportive Parenting of High-Risk Infants (CS-DSPHI): Development and Psychometric Testing
item.description: BACKGROUND: Developmentally supportive parenting (DSP) is the parental competency that optimizes developmental outcomes in high-risk infants, spanning developmental knowledge, emotional responsiveness, cognitive stimulation, and the psychological capacity to sustain these behaviors. Existing measures assess caregiving confidence or require trained observers; none captures DSP competency by self-report.

item.title: Income Dynamics and Incident Esophageal Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Higher income variability, persistently low income, and income decline over the 5-year income assessment period were independently associated with increased EC risk.

item.title: Effect of Dermal Fibroblast-Conditioned Media on Human Dermal Fibroblasts Treated With Electromagnetic Transduction Therapy
item.description: CONCLUSION: EMTT at low magnetic field strength, particularly if combined with HDFCM, promotes proliferation and migration while reducing senescence in aged HDFs. This approach may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for skin regeneration and antiaging applications, especially for aging or damaged dermal tissues.

item.title: Effects of Isthmus-Sparing Lobectomy on Thyroid Function: A Prospective, Multicenter, Comparative Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Isthmus-sparing lobectomy better preserves thyroid function and reduces postoperative subclinical hypothyroidism and hormone replacement needs compared to isthmus-removing lobectomy.

item.title: Toward O<sub>2</sub>-tolerant CO<sub>2</sub> electro-reduction for direct flue gas utilization
item.description: The electrochemical CO(2) reduction reaction (CO(2)RR) is a promising strategy for converting CO(2) into value-added chemicals. Beyond the conventional use of purified CO(2), direct flue gas utilization offers a pathway to improve the technoeconomic viability of carbon conversion by eliminating costly CO(2) purification processes. However, O(2) present in flue gas poses a major challenge, as the thermodynamically favored oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) can dominate cathodic reactions and...

item.title: Epigenomic correlates of co-morbid psychosis in 22q deletion syndrome
item.description: CONCLUSION: DNAm continues to provide new insights into 22q11DS, including psychosis risk and, in the future, may serve as a reliable predictor of co-morbidities within this broad phenotype.

item.title: When Did We Learn to See Malocclusion? Böcklin's Death, the Deviated Mandible, and the Orthodontic Eye
item.description: Arnold Böcklin's Self-Portrait with Death Playing the Fiddle (1872) is usually interpreted as a modern memento mori: the artist pauses at his work while Death plays a fiddle immediately behind him. Yet a closer anatomical inspection reveals another striking feature. Böcklin's own mouth is closed, whereas Death's skull has an open jaw that appears to deviate laterally. The skeleton seems almost to sing while playing a fiddle with only one string-the lowest G string. Although the apparent...

item.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Over-the-Counter Hearing Aids in Ageing Populations With Hearing Loss
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: OTC HAs demonstrated a performance comparable to that of prescription HAs and may serve as a cost-effective option for older adults with mild-to-moderate HL.

item.title: Broadband Electro-Thermal Full-Space Modulation in Freeform VO2 Metagrating in the Telecom Band
item.description: Electrically tunable metasurfaces for free-space light modulation have been widely studied, with VO2-based phase-change metasurfaces standing out for their large, broadband material tunability and reliable electrical modulation. However, simultaneously modulating both transmitted and reflected beams across a broad bandwidth is a multi-objective problem that is difficult to satisfy with intuitive metasurface designs built on one or a few eigenmodes, calling for complex multimode structures...

item.title: Sialic Acid-Targeting Lectin-Conjugated Oxygen Nanosomes Alleviate Hypoxia and Promote Macrophage Activation in Pancreatic Cancer Cells
item.description: CONCLUSION: Lectin-ONs integrate sialic acid-targeted delivery with oxygen-mediated hypoxia alleviation and were associated with increased macrophage TNF-α secretion in vitro. These findings support Lectin-ONs as a potential platform for modulating the hypoxic and immunosuppressive microenvironment of pancreatic cancer, although further mechanistic and in vivo validation is required.

item.title: The DentoNeural Axis: A Piezo channel-mediated mechanosensory pathway linking tooth loss to cognitive decline
item.description: BACKGROUND: Two independent meta-analyses-one of 18 cohort studies (n = 356,297) and one dose-response analysis of 14 longitudinal studies (n = 34,074)-demonstrate dose-dependent associations between tooth loss and dementia. The latter reported hazard ratio (HR) 1.48 (95% CI 1.18-1.87) for cognitive impairment and HR 1.28 (95% CI 1.09-1.49) for dementia; the former reported relative risk (RR) 1.20 and 1.15 for the same outcomes. The 2024 Lancet Commission expanded modifiable dementia risk...

item.title: Opportunistic Cardiovascular Risk Assessment in the Eye Clinic: Validation of a Retinal Deep Learning-Based 10-Year Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Estimator
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning analysis of routine retinal photographs provides cardiovascular risk stratification comparable to established clinical equations, offering a valid, noninvasive solution for opportunistic screening even when missing laboratory data precludes the standard risk calculators. These findings support the potential for opportunistic systemic risk assessment within the eye clinic, enhancing the role of the ophthalmologist in primary prevention.

item.title: Frequency and Risk Factors for Difficult-to-Treat Inflammatory Bowel Disease among Patients Receiving Advanced Therapies in a Korean Tertiary-Care Cohort
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: MF DTT-IBD occurred in one-quarter of patients. Timing of AT initiation and age in UC and therapy type and age in CD patients were key predictors. High MR DTT-IBD risk in CD patients underscores the need for proactive monitoring and early strategies.

item.title: Long-Term Outcomes According to a Device-Assisted Enteroscopy Strategy after Capsule Endoscopy in Patients with Small Bowel Bleeding: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Patients who require therapeutic DAE for SB bleeding remain at increased long-term risk of rebleeding and mortality. These findings likely reflect their greater underlying disease burden and highlight the need for individualized long-term surveillance and careful management of comorbidities, even after therapeutic intervention.

item.title: Association of waist circumference trajectories with incident chronic kidney disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: Serial WC increase may serve as a simple, clinically accessible marker of cumulative metabolic burden and future CKD risk.

item.title: Diversity and Host Associations of the Genus Colletotrichum in Korea
item.description: Colletotrichum is one of the most economically important genera of plant pathogenic fungi worldwide, yet its species diversity and host associations remain incompletely understood in many regions. In Korea, historical records based largely on morphological identification have underestimated species diversity and obscured host-association patterns. In this review, we provide an integrative reassessment of Colletotrichum diversity and host associations in Korea, combining published literature with...

item.title: Latent profiles of body composition in older adults with hypertension: associations with physical fitness and differences in blood pressure and fasting plasma glucose
item.description: CONCLUSION: Distinct body composition profiles in older adults with hypertension were associated with differences in physical fitness and cardiometabolic characteristics. These findings support the value of a person-centered approach that integrates body composition and physical fitness.

item.title: Long-term lactate ingestion and exercise training differentially modulate body composition, resting substrate metabolism, and tissue-specific metabolic remodeling in mice
item.description: CONCLUSION: Long-term lactate ingestion and exercise training produced distinct but partially overlapping systemic and molecular response patterns. Lactate ingestion was associated with lower adiposity and increased abundance of skeletal muscle proteins related to fatty acid handling and lactate transport, whereas exercise training increased carbohydrate oxidation, energy expenditure, and the abundance of proteins associated with glucose metabolism.

item.title: A complementary amino acid formulation enhances exercise-induced skeletal muscle remodeling during resistance training
item.description: CONCLUSION: The complementary amino acid formulation enhanced functional, structural, anabolic, metabolic, and redox adaptations during resistance training. These coordinated effects support its potential as a nutritional strategy for improving skeletal muscle quality during chronic resistance exercise.

item.title: Effects of Kinect-based mixed-reality exercise and deep-sea water consumption on metabolic syndrome: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings indicate the potential benefits of combining deep-sea water consumption and Kinect-based mixed-reality exercise in metabolic syndrome management.

item.title: Integrative ALS therapy: gene targeted therapy by base editing and potential exercise rehabilitation as synergistic strategies for functional recovery
item.description: CONCLUSION: Integrated rehabilitation is a crucial step in gene-targeted therapy for ALS. This strategy halts disease progression and restores neuromuscular function, thereby improving the lifespan and quality of life of patients with ALS.

item.title: Effects of morning versus evening high-intensity exercise on electroencephalographic and autonomic responses in middle-aged women
item.description: CONCLUSION: EEG- and HRV-derived neurophysiological response patterns to high-intensity exercise may vary with exercise timing. Morning high-intensity exercise may elicit greater neurophysiological responses than evening exercise, highlighting the importance of exercise timing in training strategies and recovery.

item.title: Effects of a low-protein, high-fructose corn syrup diet on skeletal muscle and bone in young adult mice: a pilot study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Chronic intake of a low-protein diet supplemented with HFCS was associated with altered skeletal muscle metabolic gene expression, with potential differences between muscle types and changes in trabecular bone microarchitecture, suggesting potential adverse effects of combined nutritional stress on musculoskeletal health.

item.title: Candidate neurobiological pathways linking physical exercise to cognition in Parkinson's disease: a hypothesis-generating translational framework
item.description: Cognitive impairment is a major nonmotor symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet effective strategies for preserving cognitive function remain limited. Although physical exercise may confer cognitive benefits, the biological pathways linking exercise to cognition in PD remain incompletely established. This narrative review presents a hypothesis-generating translational framework for 4 candidate mechanistic domains that may contribute to exercise-related cognitive effects in PD. First,...

item.title: Neurotologic and MRI Correlates of Idiopathic Acute Unilateral Audiovestibulopathy
item.description: CONCLUSION: 52% of patients with iAUAV showed positivity on precontrast 3D-FLAIR images, showing a strong association with vestibular deficits in the PC. The observed correlation between MRI and neurotologic findings may facilitate the diagnosis and differentiation of iAUAV and provide insight into its underlying pathophysiology as a frequent cause of acute audiovestibulopathy.

item.title: A Quasi-n-i-p Architecture Realized by Sequential Lamination Delivers 20.58% Efficiency in Inverted Organic Solar Cells
item.description: Inverted organic solar cells (OSCs) are promising for their enhanced operational stability; however, their power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) have lagged those of conventional devices, largely due to interfacial losses at the active layer/metal-oxide interface. Here, we develop a sequential lamination strategy to construct a quasi-n-i-p active layer comprising an acceptor-rich layer, a bulk heterojunction (BHJ) core, and a donor-rich layer. This vertically engineered architecture establishes...

item.title: Dry Mask Transfer Lithography for High-Resolution Patterning of Nanomaterials and Molecular Interfaces on Arbitrary Substrates
item.description: This study introduces dry mask transfer lithography as a versatile microfabrication strategy that integrates the patterning resolution of photolithography with the substrate adaptability of soft lithography. In this method, a photoresist mask is first patterned on an elastomeric polymer stamp and subsequently transferred onto a target substrate by thermally modulating interfacial adhesion and viscoelastic energy dissipation. The process enables high-fidelity pattern formation across a wide range...

item.title: Semantic distance for hypothesis generation in differential diagnosis: a framework to support the pivot and cluster strategy
item.description: The pivot and cluster strategy (PCS) is an emerging approach to diagnostic hypothesis generation. In this strategy, clinicians generate an initial intuitive diagnosis (the pivot) along with a cluster of diseases with similar clinical representations for systematic consideration. Although PCS was proposed to prevent diagnostic error, a knowledge gap remains in its practical implementation: existing differential diagnosis lists rely primarily on individual expertise, lacking reproducibility and...

item.title: Multidimensional vulnerabilities of informal settlements in the Urban South
item.description: Informal settlements are widespread and rapidly growing, often associated with high vulnerabilities. However, global-scale understanding on their spatial distribution and complexity of vulnerability is limited. Here, we delineate the informal settlements across a sample of 1,914 cities of the Global South by integrating Sentinel-2 imagery with deep learning models, and we explore the heterogeneity of vulnerability using Urban Informal Settlement Vulnerability Index that encompasses living...

item.title: Primary feasibility analysis of neoadjuvant chemotherapy with bevacizumab for resectable stage II/IIIA non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer: the NAVAL phase II study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative Cis, Pem, and Bev for clinical stage II/IIIA non-squamous NSCLC met the predefined feasibility criterion, with acceptable safety in this selected population. These findings provide historical insights supporting perioperative anti-vascular endothelial growth factor-based systemic intensification.

item.title: Synaptic connectome of a neurosecretory network in the Drosophila brain
item.description: Hormones mediate inter-organ signaling, which is crucial in orchestrating diverse behaviors and physiological processes, including sleep and activity, feeding, growth, metabolism, and reproduction. The pars intercerebralis and pars lateralis in insects represent major hubs that contain neurosecretory cells (NSCs) that produce various peptide hormones. To obtain insight into how hormonal signaling is regulated, we have characterized the synaptic connectome of NSCs in the adult Drosophila brain....

item.title: Model-Based Evaluation of the Warfarin-Sulfamethoxazole Drug-Drug Interaction
item.description: CONCLUSION: The proposed model supports model-based warfarin dosing during co-administration with different doses of sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim.

item.title: Board certification status and surgical outcomes after uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic anatomical pulmonary resection: a nationwide multicenter analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Board certification status was not associated with surgical procedure-related complications after U-VATS. These findings may support the implementation of U-VATS by non-board-certified surgeons within structured training systems and with appropriate intraoperative support.

item.title: Contacting next-of-kin for research consent following medico-legal autopsy: a practice-based study from Denmark
item.description: Obtaining informed consent from next-of-kin (NOK) for research use of medico-legal autopsy tissue is ethically sensitive and operationally complex. Although families may be receptive when approached appropriately, consent processes within medico-legal systems remain poorly described. This study aimed to describe response patterns, practical barriers, and experiences associated with contacting NOK for research consent following medico-legal autopsy. We conducted a retrospective evaluation of NOK...

item.title: Early-onset autosomal dominant distal renal tubular acidosis caused by a de novo SLC4A1 R589C variant with growth failure and rickets
item.description: Autosomal dominant (AD) distal renal tubular acidosis (dRTA) generally has a later onset and milder clinical course than autosomal recessive forms. However, delayed diagnosis may result in prolonged metabolic acidosis and severe growth impairment. Here we report the case of a Japanese boy with a de novo SLC4A1 (NM_000342.4):c.1765C > T (p.Arg589Cys) variant who presented with marked growth failure from 6 months of age and was diagnosed with AD-dRTA at 27 months. Because severe short stature was...

item.title: Impact of voxel size on hand dose calculations and dose-area histogram analysis for radiopharmaceutical operators
item.description: This study evaluated the impact of voxel size on three-dimensional (3D) hand dose distributions and maximum dose estimates for radiopharmaceutical operators and examined the relationship between dose-area histogram (DAH) indices and the maximum mean skin dose over 1 cm² ([Formula: see text]). Dose distributions in a hand phantom during administration with a shielded syringe containing ^(99m)Tc, ^(177)Lu, or ^(18)F were calculated using Monte Carlo simulations. The hand phantom voxel size was...

item.title: Computational Identification of IL-17 a Small-Molecule Inhibitors as Potential Therapeutics for Plaque Psoriasis Through e-Pharmacophore Screening, Molecular Docking, and Molecular Dynamics Simulation
item.description: Plaque psoriasis is a long-term skin disease driven by the immune system, impacting around 1-3% of people worldwide. Despite the availability of various treatment options, the limitations in effectiveness, side effects, and long-term response underscore the necessity for enhanced therapeutic strategies. Focusing on the interleukin-17 (IL-17) pathway offers a promising strategy for treating plaque psoriasis. In this research, established co-crystallized peptide-derived inhibitors (PDB IDs: 5HI3,...

item.title: Postoperative acute kidney injury associated with cast nephropathy and marked renal interstitial plasma cell infiltration in multiple myeloma: a case report
item.description: Multiple myeloma (MM) is frequently associated with renal impairment, most commonly due to cast nephropathy. We report a case of severe and persistent postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) in an 84-year-old man with smoldering MM who underwent posterior lumbar fixation for a lumbar burst fracture. Twelve hours after surgery, he developed profound hypotension and severe anemia due to surgical-site bleeding, followed by progressive renal dysfunction despite prompt transfusion and fluid...

item.title: Early thyroid-stimulating hormone dynamics predict outcomes in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma treated with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Early TSH dynamics and baseline APRI may be useful for exploratory risk stratification in advanced HCC treated with Atez+Bev, although these findings require validation in larger cohorts.

item.title: Primary leiomyosarcoma arising adjacent to a femoral stem following total hip arthroplasty: a case report with radiologic and histopathological correlation
item.description: Periprosthetic sarcomas associated with total hip arthroplasty (THA) are exceedingly rare, and most reported cases represent undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma or osteosarcoma. Primary leiomyosarcoma of bone is also an uncommon malignancy, accounting for less than 1% of primary malignant bone tumors. The occurrence of primary leiomyosarcoma adjacent to an orthopedic implant is therefore exceptionally rare. A 69-year-old woman presented with progressive left thigh pain 13 years after THA....

item.title: Early-Onset Gastric Varices After Fontan Completion Associated with a Pre-Existing Gastro-Renal Shunt
item.description: Gastroesophageal varices are recognized complications of Fontan-associated liver disease, but clinically significant varices have generally been reported more than 10 years after Fontan completion. The mechanisms of early variceal formation remain unclear. We report a child with tricuspid atresia who developed isolated gastric varices approximately 7 years after extracardiac Fontan completion in the presence of a pre-existing gastro-renal shunt (GRS). The patient underwent bidirectional Glenn...

item.title: Manufacturing Route-Dependent Biointerface Modulation in 3D-Printed and Conventional Dental Implant Systems
item.description: Implant manufacturing routes determine surface architecture and, consequently, modulate biointerface interactions that govern early biological responses. Although additive manufacturing has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional subtractive techniques, direct comparisons among commercially available systems remain limited. In this study, a commercially available additively manufactured dental implant was compared with four market-available conventionally machined systems to elucidate...

item.title: Psychological impact of the use of blood-based biomarkers for mild cognitive impairment in primary care
item.description: BackgroundBlood-based biomarker testing in primary care could contribute to the early diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease. The usefulness of using blood-based biomarker in the primary care has evaluated, but their psychological impact has not been examined.ObjectiveThe primary objective of this study is to investigate the psychological impact of disclosing results to patients and evaluate the changes in confidence of diagnoses by physicians. As a secondary objective, we compare the psychological...

item.title: Second-order consistency for learning chaotic dynamics via randomized Jacobian matching
item.description: Short-horizon accuracy does not ensure that a learned chaotic system has correct long-time dynamics. Trajectory (zeroth-order) matching constrains vector-field values, and Jacobian (first-order) matching constrains local tangent dynamics, but neither determines how the Jacobian varies away from supervised states. A model may be locally accurate while drifting toward spurious attractors and distorting long-time statistics. We show that second-order supervision mitigates these failures. Because...

item.title: Comparison of recovery profiles after anesthesia with remimazolam and flumazenil versus propofol for short-duration gynecological surgery: A prospective, randomized, single-blind trial
item.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to compare the recovery profiles after anesthesia with remimazolam reversed by flumazenil versus propofol among patients undergoing short-duration gynecological surgeries.MethodsIn this prospective, single-blind, randomized trial, 86 patients were assigned to either the propofol group (n = 43, received propofol and remifentanil) or the remimazolam group (n = 43, received remimazolam and remifentanil). At the end of the surgery, patients in the propofol group received 2...

item.title: Polyoxometalate-Scaffolded Perylene Diimide Dimers: Preorganization and Dynamic Charge Regulation for Enhanced and Durable Photosensitization
item.description: Precise control over both chromophore geometry and photoinduced charge dynamics is essential for engineering excited-state processes, yet achieving both simultaneously remains a major challenge. Here, we report a polyoxometalate (POM)-scaffolded strategy that integrates structural preorganization with dynamic charge regulation in perylene diimide (PDI) dimers. Rigid, redox-active lacunary POM clusters preorganize two PDIs into a tightly stacked, parallel-displaced, rotationally aligned...

item.title: Global IBS, Local Patterns: Regional Variability in Pain, Bloating, and Impact on Daily Life Among Asian/Australian and European Patients From the Aegis Epidemiology Survey
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: IBS phenotype and symptom burden differ across regions. Bloating, rather than abdominal pain, was more strongly associated with impaired quality of life, supporting symptom-centered and culturally tailored IBS management.

item.title: Editorial: Taking a Different Route-Navigating the Switch From Intravenous to Subcutaneous Vedolizumab
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Molecular, spatial, and AI-enabled technologies for predicting neoadjuvant therapy response in locally advanced rectal cancer
item.description: Pretreatment prediction of neoadjuvant response remains an unresolved challenge in locally advanced rectal cancer, where management is moving towards risk-adapted and response-oriented treatment strategies. Prediction remains difficult because response reflects interacting tumour-intrinsic, immune, stromal, and spatial processes that are incompletely captured by standard clinical and radiological assessment. From a technology-centred perspective, in this Review we assess how molecular, spatial,...

item.title: Evolutionary relationship between organellar DNA inheritance patterns and traits of seed plants
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Functional traits were associated with organelle inheritance patterns, with ecological and evolutionary implications. Similar ecological factors may be associated with the independent occurrence of paternal inheritance across lineages. Future work integrating molecular and ecological data will help elucidate the mechanisms underlying organelle inheritance and their adaptive significance.

item.title: A cross-sectional analysis of cardiometabolic and lifestyle-related profiles in men living with HIV in Japan using linked nationwide claims and health checkup data
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Among men receiving contemporary HIV care in Japan, HIV infection was associated with modest differences in BMI and dyslipidaemia but not with hypertension or diabetes mellitus.

item.title: Exploring Transdiagnostic Mechanisms Linking Borderline Personality Disorder and Disordered Eating
item.description: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) frequently co-occurs with eating disorders (EDs). Disordered eating may serve as a coping strategy to regulate emotions/manage rejection sensitivity, abandonment fears, shame, and self-disgust. Research examining disordered eating in BPD remains limited. This study explored ED pathology/related psychological constructs in adults diagnosed with BPD. Eighty participants completed questionnaires assessing BPD symptom severity, ED pathology, childhood trauma,...

item.title: What Is True for Others Does Not Apply to Me: Expectations About Social Causality and the Anticipation of Emotions in Borderline Personality Disorder
item.description: Research suggests that individuals with borderline personality disorder (BPD) display a maladaptive explanatory style, but it remains unclear whether this bias is specific to self-referential processing or reflects a broader negative tendency. We examined whether expectations about self-esteem-damaging and self-esteem-enhancing explanations, as well as associated emotions, are specific to self-referential processing in BPD, and how they relate to self-esteem and loneliness. Sixty individuals...

item.title: Multidimensional Cardiac Phenotyping of Daphnia magna Enables One-Hour Effect-Based Screening of Aquatic Toxicity
item.description: Operational water quality management relies on physicochemical monitoring and targeted chemical analysis, but routine surveillance covers only a prioritized subset of high-risk contaminants and does not capture biological activity from unmonitored chemicals, transformation products, or complex mixtures. Whole-organism bioassays provide complementary effect information, yet the conventional Daphnia magna (D. magna) acute immobilization end point requires 48 h. Here, we introduce D-HEART...

item.title: Dietary exposure and health risk assessment of perchlorate and chlorate in Shenzhen: a Monte Carlo simulation study
item.description: Perchlorate and chlorate are environmental contaminants that competitively inhibit thyroidal iodide uptake, posing health risks particularly for vulnerable populations. This study developed an isotope dilution UPLC-MS/MS method to determine perchlorate and chlorate levels in 346 samples (vegetables, fruits, eggs, and drinking water) collected from Shenzhen. Probabilistic dietary exposure assessment was conducted across 11 age-gender groups using Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations) with...

item.title: Predicting ICU Seizures Using 1 hour of cEEG
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Integrating automated IIC probabilities with quantitative background EEG features enables moderate, interpretable near-term seizure prediction from a single hour of ICU cEEG. Initial external validation on an independent multicenter ICU cohort supports generalizability, although broader prospective and multicenter evaluation are needed before clinical deployment.

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Astrocytic facilitation of somatic NMDARs underpins hippocampal E-S potentiation
item.description: EPSP-spike (E-S) potentiation is a form of plasticity defined by a persistent increase in neuronal spike output for a given synaptic input, reflecting enhanced E-S coupling independent of synaptic strength. However, its cellular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that brief induction of E-S potentiation triggers a sustained calcium activity increase in astrocytes adjacent to the hippocampal CA1 pyramidal layer. Mechanistically, E-S potentiation critically requires...

item.title: Laundering and evasion in response to antislavery policies in Brazil's cattle sector
item.description: Modern slavery remains pervasive across many economic sectors. Progress toward eradicating it has been partially hindered by a lack of tested, comprehensive policy responses. Using data on millions of cattle transactions in Brazil, we evaluated how ranchers changed their selling behavior after being added to the "Dirty List," a public registry that names and shames employers found to use modern slavery. item.title: A multiscale framework for heme crystallization inhibition: From single-molecule step-capping to parasite suppression
item.description: Heme crystallization is central to malaria parasites' survival during the erythrocytic stage of the disease, yet how clinically relevant antimalarial drugs modulate this process at the molecular level remains unclear. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In immunocompetent patients with CM-PIIRS, adjunctive corticosteroid therapy was associated with sustained improvement in neurologic, visual, and radiologic outcomes with mixed improvement in hearing after a year of therapy, with mild residual deficits.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Oral upadacitinib combined with NB-UVB phototherapy demonstrated superior short-term efficacy compared with NB-UVB alone in patients with active non-segmental vitiligo, with an acceptable safety profile. These findings support this combination as a promising therapeutic strategy and warrant further validation in larger randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up.

item.title: Development of bioinformatics competency framework to address labor market demands in Thailand
item.description: Bioinformatics plays a pivotal role in advancing healthcare, agriculture, and biotechnology. However, in Thailand, expectations regarding workforce demand and the core competencies of bioinformatics graduates remain insufficiently defined. item.title: Predictors of immunological non-response despite virological suppression in people living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy: A systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: Immunological Nonresponse (INR) in people living with HIV (PLWH) is characterized by inadequate CD4+ T-cell recovery despite effective viral suppression through antiretroviral therapy (ART). item.title: Understanding cell fate decisions with temporal attention
item.description: Understanding non-genetic determinants of cell fate is critical for developing and improving cancer therapies, as genetically identical cells can exhibit divergent outcomes under the same treatment conditions. In this work, we present a deep learning approach for cell fate prediction from raw long-term live-cell recordings of cancer cell populations under chemotherapeutic treatment. item.title: Quantifying the unique needs of women with lower limb loss: A national, cross-sectional, survey-based needs assessment
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: An important contribution of this exploratory needs assessment was its ability to identify candidate constructs that may serve as building blocks for developing a clinically relevant patient-reported outcome measure for women with lower limb loss. Future research should build on these findings to develop and validate women-specific outcome measures, ultimately supporting limb loss care teams in providing optimal, individualized care for this underserved population.

item.title: Structural and biochemical insights into HCV envelope proteins for germline-targeting vaccines
item.description: Despite effective antivirals, Hepatitis C remains a global health burden, reflecting the difficulty of eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs). item.title: Neural signatures of serial order access in verbal working memory
item.description: Serial order working memory allows information to be maintained as structured sequences, yet the neural formats supporting access to serial position remain unclear. Behavioral evidence suggests that temporal order can be recoded into spatial representations, but serial order may also rely on representations that generalize beyond the spatial configuration of encoding. item.title: GTPase GBP7 promotes HSV-1 infection by interacting with and activating eEF1A1 to accelerate the protein translation process
item.description: Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) are immune GTPases induced by interferons (IFNs) and comprise GBPs1-7. item.title: Comparative effectiveness of amlodipine versus nifedipine prescribed at discharge in patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack: A nationwide 5-year follow-up registry study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed that amlodipine, compared to nifedipine, may be associated with improved functional recovery in ischemic stroke or TIA patients. Randomized controlled trials are warranted to confirm these findings and refine CCB therapy.

item.title: Latent encoding of movement in primary visual cortex
item.description: Neurons in the primary visual cortex (V1) are classically thought to encode spatial features of visual stimuli through simple population codes: each neuron exhibits a preferred orientation and preferred spatial frequency, both of which remaining invariant to other aspects of the visual stimulus. item.description: Nuclear receptor NR1F regulates circadian rhythms in mammals, metamorphosis in insects, and molting in free-living Caenorhabditis elegans; however, its role in parasitic nematode development remains elusive. item.title: Sparse neuronal C4 elevation induces network-wide transcriptomic and lipid-droplet remodeling in the cortical microenvironment
item.description: The complement component C4 regulates synaptic refinement and plasticity in the brain and has been implicated in multiple neurological and psychiatric disorders, with especially strong genetic evidence linking elevated C4A expression to schizophrenia. item.title: Hodgkin Lymphoma With Sarcoid-Like Reaction: Importance of Clinicopathological Correlation in Granulomatous Lymphadenopathy
item.description: BACKGROUND Sarcoid-like reaction, characterized by noncaseating epithelioid granulomas, occurs in 13.8% of Hodgkin lymphoma cases. When the granulomatous component is prominent and neoplastic cells are scarce, the initial biopsy may lead to a misdiagnosis of sarcoidosis. Reliance on pathological findings alone, without integration of the clinical context, can result in considerable diagnostic delay. item.description: Hyperpolarized gas-phase MRI is an emerging diagnostic modality, with the clinical utility of hyperpolarized Xe-129 gas for functional lung imaging recently supported by FDA regulatory approval. item.title: Interfacial Cofactor Recycling Electroenzymatic Platform for Endergonic CO2 Reduction
item.description: To overcome the thermodynamic barrier of "NADH-dependent CO2 reduction", we developed a bioelectrosynthesis platform via the co-immobilization of CO2 reductase (CR) and diaphorase (DP) on a graphite electrode. item.description: Harnessing the earth-abundant N2 via photocatalysis is a sustainable route to green NH3 synthesis. item.description: Our previous immunoproteomic studies on patients with acute brucellosis identified outer membrane protein 25 (Omp25) of Brucella melitensis as one of the immunogenic antigens, indicating its potential to be used as a diagnostic marker and a tool to differentiate acute and chronic human brucellosis. item.description: Recursive splice sites are rare motifs postulated to facilitate splicing across massive introns and shape isoform diversity. The necessity of recursive splicing (RS) and its role in human disease are unsubstantiated. item.title: Proton Pump Inhibitors and Risk of Hyponatremia
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: PPI-treatment was associated with a higher risk of hyponatremia compared to treatment with histamine-2 receptor antagonists. This supports a strong independent association between use of PPIs and profound hyponatremia.

item.description: Elevated childhood blood pressure (BP) is associated with adulthood cardiovascular mortality. However, evidence of an association between maternal and perinatal factors and standardized childhood BP percentiles in Japan remains limited. item.description: OBJECTIVE: Sleep disorders are frequent but undercharacterized comorbidities in developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs). We aimed to estimate the frequency, spectrum, and burden of sleep disturbances across genetic DEE subtypes using real-world data extracted from electronic health records (EHRs) through natural language processing (NLP).

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study established a treatment-sensitive network based on the whole-brain connectome. These findings provide valuable empirical evidence for identifying biomarkers for IGD treatment and advance personalised therapeutic strategies.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this registry-based study of US heart transplant candidates, a US-CRS-based allocation system prioritized sicker candidates with higher mortality without transplant compared with the current medical urgency statuses.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In 2 randomized clinical trials including a demographically diverse sample of US adults, learning about common uncertainties with a new cancer drug's benefits and risks reduced hypothetical decisions to take the drug.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this multicenter study of patients hospitalized for alcohol withdrawal syndrome, there were no differences in hospital length of stay or the need for invasive mechanical ventilation between initiation of phenobarbital vs diazepam. These results may suggest near therapeutic equivalence between phenobarbital and long-acting benzodiazepines.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this discrete choice experiment of older adults in Beijing, influenza vaccination preferences were associated with vaccine profiles, trusted communication, and community-based service delivery. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A single dose of MenACYW-TT induced robust immunogenicity against all four serogroups and demonstrated an acceptable safety profile across all age groups of Vietnamese participants. item.description: CONCLUSION: Nanoplatform-mediated TAM reprogramming has developed into a rapidly expanding interdisciplinary research area linking nanoplatform engineering, macrophage-directed regulation, and tumor microenvironment remodeling. item.title: Co-occurrence of viral respiratory pathogens: prevalence, seasonal distribution, and symptomatology in outpatients in Bavaria, Germany, from April 2025 - March 2026
item.description: CONCLUSION: The frequency of multi-infections follows the seasonality of the corresponding viruses. Especially children under 5 years of age are affected by co-infections. Among the studied viruses, influenza A showed the lowest relative rate of co-detection, in line with its pronounced seasonality - a pattern that warrants further investigation.

item.title: Healthcare pathways and outpatient management prior to community-acquired sepsis hospitalization in Germany, 2016-2019
item.description: CONCLUSION: Most patients with CAS had healthcare contact in the week prior to hospitalization, predominantly in outpatient care. The frequent encounters shortly before admission and low rates of anti-infective prescription may suggest opportunities for earlier recognition and better risk stratification, e.g. by strengthening sepsis awareness and diagnostic strategies in outpatient settings.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Neighborhood-level social determinants were associated with reduced continuity of ambulatory surgical care, reflected by lower longitudinal laser treatment intensity, suggesting structural influences on continuity of ambulatory surgical care rather than biologic disease trajectory.

item.description: L929 cells exhibit relatively strong resistance to infection by Nelson Bay orthoreovirus (NBV), primarily due to the unique virus-host interaction that suppresses NBV infection at multiple stages, including viral entry, genome replication, and virion assembly. item.description: Scientific independence alone does not create a sustainable research program. item.title: BdPiwi is essential for gametogenesis and post-embryonic development in the oriental fruit fly, Bactrocera dorsalis
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that BdPiwi is a pleiotropic regulator governing gonadogenesis, fertility, and metamorphic transition in B. dorsalis. This study expands the functional repertoire of Piwi genes in insect pests and provides a promising molecular target for genetic-based management of this devastating invasive species. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
